justifications.functional_suitability: All functional requirements are thoroughly supported: Customer Portal Container enables online claims submission (R-01), Adjuster Web App Container provides dedicated adjuster tooling (R-02), and Routing Rules Manager combined with Claims Orchestrator Container enables granular, claim-type-by-claim-type migration (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: To beat the 5s mainframe latency and achieve sub-2s screen loads (R-05), the architecture employs Reference Data Cache Client (Redis), Client-Side Cache & State Manager (TanStack Query/IndexedDB), and asynchronous decoupling via Azure Service Bus and Transactional Outbox.
justifications.compatibility: Coexistence with the COBOL/DB2 mainframe is handled by Legacy Mainframe Adapter Container using CICS/MQ translation over ExpressRoute. Azure Service Bus explicitly queues requests during the unextendable 23:00-05:00 batch window to prevent mainframe interference.
justifications.usability: Both End Customers & Brokers and Claims Adjusters have purpose-built web interfaces. Adjuster Web App Container includes Draft Persistence Manager and optimistic UI patterns for productivity, though specific portal differentiations between brokers and customers are not detailed.
justifications.reliability: R-04 consistency is rigorously ensured using Transactional Store Component with Outbox Table Component, MassTransit Saga Workflow Orchestrator, and State & Idempotency Manager in the mainframe adapter to guarantee exactly-once processing and zero data loss.
justifications.security: Authentication Validator in API Gateway enforces Entra ID SSO via OIDC (R-07). mTLS Security Handler manages certificates and legacy RACF credentials over ExpressRoute, while Azure Key Vault securely manages customer keys and application secrets.
justifications.maintainability: One-day rollback (R-06) is achieved via Routing Rules Manager, Azure App Configuration dynamic feature flags, and Versioned State Schema Component. Clear separation of concerns is maintained with an Anti-Corruption Layer (Legacy Mainframe Adapter Container).
justifications.portability: The hybrid topology (azure-westeurope and on-premise) is cleanly mapped using containerized services (Azure Container Apps) and ExpressRoute. However, high coupling to proprietary Azure PaaS (App Configuration, Service Bus, Cosmos DB) restricts cloud-neutral portability.

PERF-01.justification: While Redis reference caching and UI client-side caching exist, the architecture lacks an explicit read-replication or proactive sync mechanism for active claim data residing primarily on the mainframe.
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratios for claim records residing on the legacy mainframe
Overhead of synchronous backend hops across hybrid ExpressRoute connections
tradeoffs: Serving stale cached adjuster data versus incurring 5-second synchronous mainframe roundtrips

PERF-02.justification: Asynchronous ingestion via Azure Service Bus and the Transactional Outbox pattern fully decouples frontend submissions from mainframe processing, buffering surges without impacting batch windows.
sensitivity_points: Azure Service Bus queue depth capacity during month-end traffic spikes
Database write throughput under five-times ingestion load
tradeoffs: Immediate customer submission acceptance at the expense of eventual consistency with backend systems

AVAIL-01.justification: Azure Service Bus and the Transactional Outbox explicitly queue claims when the mainframe batch window is active, allowing continuous ingestion and automated deferred forwarding.
sensitivity_points: Message time-to-live settings during extended six-hour batch windows
Reliability of outbox publisher relaying queued messages
tradeoffs: Maintained platform availability during batch windows trading off real-time mainframe confirmation

AVAIL-02.justification: The Saga orchestrator (MassTransit) combined with the Outbox table and dedicated State & Idempotency Manager in the adapter container guarantees exactly-once processing and robust reconciliation.
sensitivity_points: Deterministic correlation IDs across legacy mainframe MQ/CICS and modern services
Storage performance of Cosmos DB idempotency records
tradeoffs: Strong exactly-once semantics achieved at the cost of additional idempotency datastore roundtrips

MOD-01.justification: Routing Rules Manager via Azure App Configuration, feature flags, versioned schemas, and an anti-corruption adapter allow declarative claim-type routing and instantaneous single-day rollbacks.
sensitivity_points: Propagation latency of feature flag changes across distributed gateway instances
Backward compatibility of schema versioning during rollback
tradeoffs: Dynamic routing flexibility introduces operational complexity in configuration management

MOD-02.justification: UIs interact solely with the API Gateway and Orchestrator. The anti-corruption adapter decouples legacy boundaries, allowing retirement of the mainframe without changes to UI layers.
sensitivity_points: Strict adherence of UI contracts to domain APIs rather than mainframe schema models
Cutover completeness of Claims State Database as system of record
tradeoffs: Maintaining abstraction layer overhead throughout migration to avoid eventual frontend rewrites

SEC-01.justification: Authentication validator and domain rules engine enforce validation and audit logging, though granular broker-to-claim authorization (ABAC/RBAC) rules are not fully articulated.
sensitivity_points: Enforcement of tenant/broker scoping claims inside OIDC access tokens
Completeness of immutable audit log generation on rejected requests
tradeoffs: Fine-grained runtime attribute checks increase request processing latency at the domain layer

SEC-02.justification: Authentication is centralized in Microsoft Entra ID; revoking access cuts off UI and API entry points. However, token caching and existing OIDC access token TTLs must be configured below 15 minutes.
sensitivity_points: Default access token expiration and Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) support in Entra ID
Session invalidation propagation speed across the BFF layer
tradeoffs: Short-lived tokens improve revocation speed but increase authentication refresh overhead
